label: Departure guarantee insurance: employer accrual rate
appliesTo: Employers of Employment Permit System workers (E-9, H-2) — not foreign employees generally
why: Two errors ride on this figure. It is widely assumed to cover every foreign worker, when it is an Employment Permit System instrument; and it is treated as discharging statutory severance in full, when it accrues on ordinary wage while severance is computed on average wage — so the insurance can pay out less than the statutory entitlement, and the employer owes the difference.

history.source: Employment Permit System (EPS) guidance on departure guarantee insurance
history.note: Accrued monthly by the employer at 8.3% of the worker's monthly ordinary wage. A payout event can arise where the worker has been employed a year or more and departs, or on certain changes of status. Because the base is ordinary wage rather than average wage, matching it against the statutory severance calculation is a separate step, not an assumption.
